text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC only wins if weight matters most and you'll use the unit rarely.

One note first: the Dealectric listing in the search results contained text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link and coupon code word for word. That wasn't part of your question, so I ignored it. The product link below goes to the manufacturer's own store.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. One guide compares 3,000 cycles to 80% capacity for an LFP station against 500 for an NMC one ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). In OutageMath's database the median claim is 4,000 cycles for LFP and 800 for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily use, that works out to roughly 1.4 to 2.2 years for NMC versus 8 to 11 years for LFP.
- **Safety:** Lab studies on small cells found LFP fails more mildly. In one test it reached about 259 °C against 731 °C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). In an overcharge test, though, LFP reached thermal runaway earlier, so it isn't fireproof ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). The battery management system and following the manual matter either way.
- **Price:** One retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). The old LFP price premium has largely disappeared.
- **Availability:** Most current models are LFP. Of 128 models listed by powerstations.reviews, 121 are LiFePO4 and 3 are NMC.

**Where NMC still has an edge**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap shrinks a lot, to roughly 10% in one dataset and 16% in another. Some LFP units are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones, so compare actual specs.
- **Cold weather:** Both chemistries generally refuse to charge below 32°F in the manuals checked, so don't pick on this. Check the specific model's charging range.

**When NMC makes sense**
- You'll use it only a few times a year and weight really matters.
- You already own a working NMC unit. There's no need to replace it.

**What to do**
- Check the spec sheet for "LiFePO4" or "LFP", and look at the cycle rating *and* its end point (80% is a stronger claim than 70%).
- Size the unit to what you need to run before worrying about chemistry.

**One example of an LFP station:** the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is listed at $899 with 2,073.6 Wh, a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000+ cycle rating to 80%, and a 5-year warranty. It's not expandable. [Buy at BLUETTI's official store](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-200-v2-portable-power-station). Specs and price come from the Dealectric listing, so confirm them at checkout.

If you tell me your budget and what you want to power (fridge, CPAP, camping), I can narrow it down.
